svg.title: Weather Command — mission desk and responsive design, version 1
svg.desc: Original interface concept showing desktop, tablet, phone, and post-forecast debrief layouts. Map pressure is shown only as station readings and tendency, never as invented isobars.
svg.text: WEATHER COMMAND / ORIGINAL DESIGN BOARD / V1
Forecast desk — evidence first, uncertainty visible
Figma import source · desktop, tablet, phone, and debrief · built from the real mission flow and current science model

g.text: Forecast when the main change will reach Central Station. Use the evidence; explain your range.
Schematic region · every map mark has a text equivalent below
Station pressure is labeled in hPa
Select a row to inspect the complete reading and the same station’s trend
Advance time to reveal pressure and temperature trends. Values shown are the published scenario start state.
Step through evidence at your own pace
At least two readings are needed for a trend.
For Central Station · ranges keep uncertainty visible
Choose the plan your forecast supports ▾
Forecast the change at Central Station.
Forecast window 30–180 min · ranges keep uncertainty visible
More ranges continue below · compare unlocks only after the window closes.

svg.text: 02 TABLET · 768 × 1024 · STACK MAP, READINGS, AND FORECAST
03 PHONE · 390 × 844 · PROGRESSIVE PANELS + FIXED TIME ACTION

g.text: Read the forecast beside the record. The explanation matters as much as the range.
Ranges can be defensible without exact matches
Values here illustrate layout and will be bound to a qualified mission record before release.
Your confidence fits the width of your range
This is feedback about the forecast, not a grade on you.
Guided debrief · why the forecast changed
Pressure fell as the boundary approached.
West changed first; Central was next in sequence.
Widen timing, cite the station sequence, compare again.

svg.text: 04 DEBRIEF · 1440 × 900 · SIDE-BY-SIDE RECORD, DIMENSIONAL FEEDBACK, RECOVERY ALWAYS AVAILABLE
Design rules: 44 px minimum controls · focus ring #FFD166 · text labels + patterns, never color alone · reduced motion removes interpolation · no live-weather implication.
